                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And Saul sought to smite David even to the wall with the javelin: but he slipt away out of Sauls presence; and he smote the javelin into the wall: and David fled, and escaped that night.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 59. title.</ns0:note> Saul also sent messengers unto David's house to watch him, and to slay him in the morn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Why not in the Night? <ns0:hi>Ans.</ns0:hi> Partly, because it would have been barbarous, and most dishonourable to <ns0:hi>Saul,</ns0:hi> to break into <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s House by Night, and kill him in his own House and Bed; and it seemed more expedient to kill him as he came out of his House in the Morning: partly, because the Night might give <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> some opportunity of escaping, which the Day-light would prevent: and principally, by Gods singular Providence, infatuating <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi>'s mind to take the worst course, that <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> might be delivered from him.</ns0:note>: and Michal Davids wife told him, saying, If thou save not thy life to night, to morrow thou shalt be slain <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Which she might learn, either by information from <ns0:hi>Iona<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />than,</ns0:hi> or some other Courtier that was privy to the design: or from her own observation of some suspicious or danger<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous Persons hovering about the House.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 ¶ So Michal let David down thorow a win<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dow <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Because they lay in wait for him at the Doors of the House, whensoever he should come forth there.</ns0:note>: and he went and fled, and escaped.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And Michal took <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">

                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> an image <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>Teraphim,</ns0:hi> which was an Image made in human shape: which she might keep secretly, either out of a super<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stitious regard to it, or out of meer curiosity. This stratagen<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> she used, because knowing her Fathers unquiet, and jealous, and furious temper, she suspected he might come or send, to see whether <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> was there or no.</ns0:note>, and laid <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> in the bed, and put a pillow of goats <ns0:hi>hair for</ns0:hi> his bolster <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>put great Goats</ns0:hi> hair upon <ns0:hi>his Bolster,</ns0:hi> i. e. upon the head and face of the Image, which lay upon his Bolster, that it might have some kind of resemblance of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s head and hair, at least in a sick man's Bed, where there useth to be but a glimmer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing light. <ns0:hi>Goats</ns0:hi> is here put for <ns0:hi>Goats hair,</ns0:hi> as it manifestly is, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 25. 4. and 26. 7. and 35. 26. It is acknowledged by Learned Writers, that in those Eastern Countries, Goats had much longer hair than ours have, and were shorn like Sheep; and that their hair was not unlike to a Mans or Womans hair; as may also be gathered from <ns0:hi>Cant.</ns0:hi> 4. 1. <ns0:hi>thy hair is as a flock of Goats,</ns0:hi> i. e. as the hair of a flock of Goats. And as there was Goats hair of several colours, (as the Wool of Sheep in divers parts is of very differing colours, as white, or black, or yellow, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>) so it is most probable <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>he took that colour which was likest the colour of <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s hair. And she took this rather than the hair of another man, because the procuring and ordering of that would have taken up some time; whereas she had Goats hair of all sorts at hand, as being used in Spinning or Weaving, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Or, the sense may be this, according to our Translation, That she put a Pillow of the softest part of Goats hair under the head of the Image, as they used to put under the heads of sick Men; whereby also the head of the Image sinking into the Pillow, might be less discerned, especially when it was either wholly or in part covered with a Cloath. And all this art was used, that <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> being supposed, and, by some Persons who were sent to inquire, perceived, as they thought, to be in the Bed, <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> might be hindred from pursuing and overtaking him be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore he had got into some secure place.</ns0:note>, and covered <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> with a cloth <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Upon pretence of his being sick, and needing some such covering, but really in design to prevent the discovery of her deceit.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 And when Saul sent messengers <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">To wit, other Messengers in the Morning, supposing the former to be either slow or perfidious.</ns0:note> to take Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid, she said, He <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> sick.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">15 And Saul sent the messengers <ns0:hi>again</ns0:hi> to see Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Or onely, <ns0:hi>to see David,</ns0:hi> which they did not before, but went away satisfied (as it was fit they should) with her Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />port and Testimony of his sickness.</ns0:note>, saying, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 And when the messengers were come in, behold, <ns0:hi>there was</ns0:hi> an image in the bed, with a pil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />low of goats <ns0:hi>hairjor</ns0:hi> his bolster.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And Saul said unto Michal, Why hast thou deceived me so, and sent away mine enemy, that he is escaped? And Michal answered Saul, He said unto me, Let me go: Why should I kill thee <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">If thou dost not permit me to escape without discove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry, I shall be forced for my own defence to kill thee. Though it is most likely, this was a lye, and a fiction of her own.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 ¶ So David fled, and escaped, and came to Samuel to Ramah <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Partly, for comfort and direction in his grert distress; and partly, for safety, supposing that <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> would be ashamed to execute his Bloody designs in the presence of so venera<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble a Person as <ns0:hi>Samuel,</ns0:hi> who had laid so great obligations upon <ns0:hi>Saul,</ns0:hi> and had such great and just Reputation with the People.</ns0:note>, and told him all that Saul had done to him: and he and Samuel went and dwelt in Naioth.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And it was told Saul, saying, Behold, David <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> at Naioth in Ramah <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>near Ramah;</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> preposition <ns0:hi>beth, in,</ns0:hi> being oft put for <ns0:hi>near,</ns0:hi> as it is apparently used, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 33. 37, 38. <ns0:hi>Ios.</ns0:hi> 5. 13. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 20. 2. and 32. 7. <ns0:hi>Naioth</ns0:hi> was either an House or Colledge in the Town of <ns0:hi>Ramah,</ns0:hi> or a Village in the Ter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ritory of <ns0:hi>Ramah,</ns0:hi> or near to the Town of <ns0:hi>Ramah;</ns0:hi> in which there was a Colledge of the Prophets, amongst whom <ns0:hi>Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />muel</ns0:hi> thought <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> might be secure.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:236" />20 And Saul sent messengers to take David <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Thus <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi>'s wickedness and fury increased; and he that at first used onely secret practices against <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> now breaks forth into open and impudent Hostilities; plainly declaring, that he neither feared God, nor reverenced Man. He would have punished <ns0:hi>Samuel,</ns0:hi> as afterwards he did <ns0:hi>Abimeleck,</ns0:hi> for giving <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> entertainment, but that he feared the People, who had so great and unanimous a Veneration for him.</ns0:note>: and when they saw the company of the Prophets prophesying <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Speaking of God, or of the things of God by Divine inspiration; either praising God, or instructing Men. Compare <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 11. 25. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 10. 5.</ns0:note>, and Samuel standing <ns0:hi>as</ns0:hi> appointed over them <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">To instruct, moderate and direct them in those Holy exercises. For though they prophesied by Divine Inspiration, which <ns0:hi>Samuel</ns0:hi> could not govern; yet they were both to prepare and dispose themselves for it be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore-hand, and to make good improvement of it afterwards, in both which they needed <ns0:hi>Samuel</ns0:hi>'s counsel and assistance. And whereas some might falsly pretend to those Raptures; or the Devil might transform himself into an Angel of Light, and convey some Evil or false Suggestions into some of their minds, <ns0:hi>Samuel</ns0:hi>'s presence and judgment was necessary to pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vent and to detect such Impostures. Besides, <ns0:hi>Samuel</ns0:hi> would by his present conjunction with them in those Holy Exercises, encourage them, and stir up others to the coveting of those Gifts, and the performance of such Religious Duties.</ns0:note>, the Spirit of God was upon the mes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sengers of Saul, and they also prophesied <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Inspired by God to do so, as wicked <ns0:hi>Balaam</ns0:hi> also was; that being wrapt up into such an extasie, their minds might be wholly taken up with those matters, and quite taken off from their design of seizing <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And when it was told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they prophesied likewise: and Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phesied also.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 Then went he also to Ramah, and came to a great well that <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in Sechu: and he asked, and said, Where <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> Samuel and David <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">For, his Messengers not returning, he knew not exactly where they were.</ns0:note>? And <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> said, Behold, <ns0:hi>they be</ns0:hi> at Naioth in Ramah.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="23">23 And he went thither to Naioth in Ramah: and the Spirit of God was upon him also <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">It came upon him in the way; whereas it came not up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on his Messengers till they came to the place. Whereby God would convince <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> of the vanity of all his designs against <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and that in them he Fought against God him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self.</ns0:note>, and he went on, and prophesied until he came to Naioth in Ramah:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="24">24 And he stript off his clothes <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">To wit, his Military or Royal Garments: which he did, either that he might suit himself and his habit to the rest of the Company; or, because his mind being altogether taken up with Divine things, he did not understand nor heed what he did.</ns0:note> also <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">This implies, that the Messengers which he sent, who probably were Military persons, had done so before him.</ns0:note>, and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phesied before Samuel <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">This doth not contradict 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 15. 35. where it is said, that <ns0:hi>Samuel came no more to see Saul:</ns0:hi> for here <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> goes to <ns0:hi>Samuel,</ns0:hi> and that not with design to see him, but to surprize <ns0:hi>David.</ns0:hi>

                     <ns0:hi>Is</ns0:hi> Saul also among the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The same Proverb which was taken up upon a like occasion, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 10. 12. is here re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />membred and revived upon this new occasion, as an Evi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence of Gods wonderful care over <ns0:hi>David;</ns0:hi> he made <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> in some sort a Prophet, that he might make <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> a King.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
